name: Priya Raman
headline: Backend engineer — data-heavy systems, streaming, and the boring reliability work
note: Every bullet below is the ground truth for this project. Nothing the agent writes is allowed to go beyond it.

bullets.text: Rebuilt shipment-status ingest from a nightly batch job into a Kafka stream, cutting status lag from 6 hours to 90 seconds for 40000 daily consignments.
Owned the PostgreSQL fleet through a major-version upgrade with 4 minutes of planned downtime, after rehearsing the cutover twice against a restored snapshot.
Introduced consumer-lag alerting and a replay tool after a partition rebalance silently dropped 3 hours of events; mean time to detection fell from 2 days to 11 minutes.
Moved 14 services from hand-managed AWS consoles into Terraform, so environments could be rebuilt from scratch in about 25 minutes.
Mentored 3 junior engineers through their first on-call rotations and wrote the runbook set the team still uses.
Built the reporting API that served 120 client dashboards, holding p95 latency under 400ms by moving aggregate rollups into materialised views.
Replaced a tangle of cron jobs with Airflow DAGs, which made failures visible and cut the weekly manual-rerun burden from about 5 hours to under 30 minutes.
Wrote the data-retention tooling that let the company answer deletion requests within the 30-day window, working from the legal team's specification.
Shipped the invoice-export feature end to end, from the Postgres schema through to the JavaScript front end.
Cut the test suite from 22 minutes to 6 by removing database round-trips from unit tests.

open_source.text: Maintains a small open-source library for safe PostgreSQL partition rotation, used by 40 or so repositories.

preferences.notes: Happy to mentor and lead projects; not looking for a people-management role.
